statement: The nonloop rank-three extension order complex is homotopy equivalent to S^2; new-element reorientation acts freely and its quotient is homotopy equivalent to RP^2 via the specified equivariant contraction map.
notes: The quotient uses explicit equivariance and covering-space Whitehead, not an arbitrary sphere equivalence. Only the new labelled element is reoriented.

statement: The opposite extension poset is the face poset of an embedded regular CW complex with ordinary nu-cubes and parallel polygonal two-cells; after quotient by new-element reorientation F(-1)=1-n.
notes: All 3^nu refinements and all 2^nu stable generizations occur. Principal-ideal cones prove closed-cell embeddings. Finite intervals independently checked by extension_compare_cells.py.

statement: For every old vertex v, the alternating sum over ordinary positions through v is mu(v); consequently F'(-1)=sum_v mu(v)=sum_i n_i.
depends_on: E1; E2; Sturmfels-Ziegler 1993 Lemma3.2 and Proposition4.2
notes: Restriction to a full inverse image retains the verified Babson fibers and upward slices. All fixed-vertex sums checked in five simple examples.

statement: The extension quotient punctured at its n regular parallel points is homotopy equivalent relative to its labelled peripheral circles to RP^2 minus n disks; replacing the disks by Mobius bands gives B(M) homotopy equivalent to the connected sum of n+1 projective planes.
notes: Explicit sector maps, meridian cuts, circle homeomorphisms, equivariance, and cofibration gluing supply the marked comparison. An unmarked sphere theorem alone would be insufficient.

statement: For the manuscript surface X_2, chi(X)=1-n-4 sum_{k>=1} k c_{2k+1}; its nonorientable crosscap number is n+1+4 sum_{k>=1} k c_{2k+1}. It is homotopy equivalent to B(M) exactly when no ordinary position has three old vertices.
notes: T3 verifies all surface and counting hypotheses where used. The condition is automatic for n<=5; the six-line certificate has c3=10 and chi=-45, refuting L1.

statement: L2 is false: all stable descendants occur. The dual surface embeds as selected incidence diamonds and entire flag-subdivided Mobius bands in B(M), containing its whole one-skeleton; comparison maps and every relative-cell attachment are explicit.
depends_on: T1; T2; T3; E2; E4; E5; finite certificates in sections/counts.tex
notes: The inclusion induces a surjection on pi1 with kernel normally generated by unselected diamond boundaries. B is obtained by adding 2F''(1)-F'(1)+b squares and (2^k/k!)F^(k)(1) k-cells for k>=3. The inclusion is equality when c3=0. Full finite comparison and eight-descendant witness in extension_compare_cells_output.json. No classical citation specifically stating this selector was found in the recorded search.

statement: Matching-sign enumeration is exhaustive for nonparallel single-element extensions of a simple uniform rank-three oriented matroid
notes: Full signed basis-exchange checker independent of GP filter

statement: Explicit simple six-line arrangement has an added line through v12 v34 v56
notes: Integer determinant and cross-product certificate

statement: Boundary packets and ordinary or exceptional transitions admit the stated exact signed tests
notes: All hypotheses hold for finite inputs

statement: The test arrangement has V360 E720 F315 and surface homeomorphic to 47 projective planes
notes: Complete gluing and local-link certificate; refutes universal chi=1-n

statement: A six-line convex-dual input gives a surface homeomorphic to 23 projective planes
notes: Topology depends on the arrangement at fixed n

statement: The fixed straight realization has 229 non-supercritical positions and corner count234
notes: Distinguished from unrestricted pseudoline count315 and360

statement: An added non-supercritical pseudoline through nu vertices requires n>=2nu
depends_on: At most one intersection per pair of pseudolines
notes: Three-vertex phenomenon first possible at n6

statement: Finite tame chord systems with pairwise single transverse crossings and equivalence of disjointness reconstruct relative positions; with one equivalence class the two-packet condition is necessary and sufficient.
notes: The abbreviated two-condition version is false for a one-class degenerate chord system. That case cannot arise from a nontrivial old arrangement.

statement: The literal labelled deployed signed polygon determines the non-supercritical relative position in the fixed arrangement.
depends_on: P4 pair extraction; chirotope uniqueness; BKMS2002 Theorems 4-5
notes: No externally supplied packet decomposition is needed: endpoint nonalternation recovers its classes. The only new-element ambiguity is reorientation.

statement: Label negation is the half-turn followed by reversal within each cluster; it is the half-turn exactly in stable positions.
depends_on: Local finite-star straightening; explicit signed expansion
notes: Includes a three-line exact counterexample to literal antipodality in a nonstable position and an expansion formula used by the counts workstream.

statement: The image consists exactly of the words whose combined old/new signs satisfy the chirotope axioms, have no zero contraction row, and agree with the canonical cluster expansion.
depends_on: RGZpreprint CHI1-CHI2; BKMS2002 representation; GP2021 Theorem 6.5 explicitly dualized; P3
notes: Complete finite image criterion; handles all multiplicities and any number of vertices on the new line. The support-matroid axiom is retained in the presence of zeros.

statement: The 2n weight rule, cluster reversal, and three candidate triangles tested against every old line do not characterize the image.
depends_on: Exact six-line moment-curve determinant and Grassmann-Pluecker certificate
notes: Candidate word (1,2,-3,-4,-6,-5,-1,-2,3,4,6,5) has exactly three local triangle candidates and total weight 12 but violates a GP relation.

statement: The full polygon image reconstructs all positions and ordinary/corridor arrows, their directions, weights and cyclic incidences, and with the prescribed transition rule the cellular embedding.
depends_on: P2; P4; local resolution; rank-two localization; signed rotation-system construction
notes: Face order four and embedding of the original large disks remain separate A.1 results; they are not inferred from the graph reconstruction.

statement: Independent local resolutions at distinct old vertices on a non-supercritical new line form the full sign cube, with distinct fully resolved positions.
depends_on: Disjoint vertex disks; disjoint supporting line sets; localization uniqueness
notes: This proves commuting squares at distinct apices; it is not by itself the complete corner theorem.

statement: For a line through exactly one old vertex, each adjacent lune either exposes an ordinary specialization fan on its half-circle or is a corridor.
depends_on: SZ1993 graph pp.30-31, Proposition 3.9 p.33, proof of Corollary 4.5 p.40; source-star separation
notes: Uses g=d and objective f=i, so no auxiliary infinity pseudoline or unproved chart extension is required. Supplies the same-apex generization corner gate in A.1.

statement: Repeated-vertex gen-gen gaps contain a specialization or an exceptional corridor
notes: Finite acyclic program and exposed fan proof; multiple vertices allowed

statement: Every all-ordinary corner circuit is a four-cycle with four distinct relative positions
notes: Tracks the prescribed reflected endpoints; no bound on the number of specializations

statement: X_2 is a compact connected nonorientable surface with embedded closed cells and s2=F(1), s1=2Fprime(1)+2b, s0=Fprime(1)+b
notes: Explicit flag circuits, Mobius bands, links and no-zigzag embeddings

statement: L4 literal tether/chord identification is false; proper chords with a marked point correspond to pairs of interior-to-boundary tethers
notes: Typed-arc counterexample, not a model of unspecified 1986 axioms; both readings of the doubtful negation covered
